question: How many postal ballots will Correos report as admitted for Spain's 29 November 2026 general election in the most recent figure it publishes on or before 26 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: The reference class is Spanish general elections held outside summer. November 2019 had 918k applications admitted and about 0.9-1.0M ballots, and April 2019 had 1.24M ballots; the July 2023 record of 2.47M was a summer-holiday outlier. 2026 points down: Vox and Ayuso are urging in-person voting, Valencia had only about 15k applications by 1 Nov (roughly 130k nationally scaled), and Andalusia's May 2026 applications were flat against 2022 (+1.1%). It points up on political salience and routine online applications. Correos usually publishes the near-final count on or right after the deposit deadline (25 Nov), so the figure should be complete; there is a small risk that only an early partial count is out by 26 Nov. No national application count had been published as of 16 Nov. No human market found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi, bookmakers).
calls.dossier:
- Correos press room (checked 2026-11-16): 29N releases so far are 6 Oct (application window opens), 10 Nov (procedures; ballot mailing began 9 Nov), and 16 Nov (application deadline reminder for 19 Nov). None contains a cumulative application or ballot count.
- Herqles, 2026-11-16: the Interior Ministry has published no aggregate postal-vote data, although Correos reports to it daily. PP and Vox asked the Junta Electoral Central (JEC) to require data sharing; no ruling yet. In 2023, about 600k applications were public 40 days out and more than 2.3M by mid-July.
- moncloa.com, 2026-11-01: about 15,000 applications in the Comunitat Valenciana (all 3 provinces) by 1 Nov, day ~26 of a ~45-day window. The article notes the bulk usually arrives in the final two weeks. The region holds about 11% of the national electorate.
- Correos Andalusia, May 2026: 178,540 applications (+1.11% vs 2022) and 163,510 ballots admitted (91.58% of applications). Ballot figure published 14 May, the day after the 13 May deposit deadline.
- 10 Nov 2019 general election: Correos admitted 918,455 applications. On the deposit deadline day (8 Nov) it reported 900,188 ballots sent; the final total was about 0.9-1.0M ballots.
- April 2019: 1,241,716 ballots admitted. July 2023: 2,622,808 applications and 2,471,935 ballots (94.2%); the 2023 interim figure was 2,461,284 on the night of the deadline.
- Since 2008, 6-9% of applicants have not cast a postal ballot.
- Vox's Abascal and Madrid's Ayuso urged in-person voting (Infobae, 2026-10-05). PP is demanding guarantees.
- Status quo: Correos issues a ballots-admitted release on the deposit deadline day (25 Nov) or the day after.
- Resolves off the headline national cumulative ballots figure (admitted/sent/deposited) in the latest Correos release dated <=26 Nov 2026 (Madrid time), not application counts.
- Event window: release must be dated on or before 26 Nov 2026; deposit deadline 25 Nov. As of 16 Nov, no ballot figure exists yet.
- Searched for but not found: any national 2026 application count, interim ballot counts, or prediction markets (none on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers).
calls.reference_class: Correos ballots-admitted totals for Spanish general elections held outside summer (2015-2019), adjusted for the 2023 step-up

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Correos-reported admitted postal ballots in Spanish general elections outside summer (Apr 2019 1.24M; Nov 2019 ~0.9M sent by deadline day; 2015/16 roughly 1.0-1.4M). July 2023's 2.47M was holiday-driven and not representative of a November vote. Early signal: ~15k applications in the Valencian Community by 1 Nov (10.8% of census) scales to about 140k nationally at day 26 of 44, a modest pace, though most applications come in the final two weeks. Upward pressures: snap-election salience and growing familiarity with postal voting. Downward pressures: Vox urging voters not to vote by post and PP distrust messaging. Correos normally publishes a near-final figure on the deposit-deadline day (25 Nov) or the day after, inside the cutoff; there is a small risk the latest release is only an interim count. No prediction market on this quantity was found (Polymarket/Kalshi only price the PM outcome; nothing on Manifold or bookmakers).

- Resolves off Correos' headline national cumulative ballots admitted/sent/deposited figure in its latest release dated on or before 26 Nov 2026 (Madrid time), not applications (solicitudes).
- Event window: release dates up to 26 Nov 2026. The deposit period that produces the count runs ~9 Nov to 25 Nov; as of 16 Nov about 40% of that deposit period has elapsed.

calls.reference_class: Correos-reported admitted/sent postal ballots in non-summer Spanish general elections 2015-2019

calls.reasoning: No 29N figures published yet (Correos releases 6 Oct, 10 Nov, 16 Nov contain no counts; Interior not releasing data). Base rate: non-summer general elections drew 0.9-1.36M ballots admitted (Jun 2016 ~1.36M, Apr 2019 1.24M, Nov 2019 ~0.9M); July 2023's 2.47M was a summer-holiday surge. Recent regional elections show flat postal usage vs comparable prior standalone elections (Andalusia 2026 +1.1%). Up: high-salience snap election, online application habit. Down: late-November date, Vox urging supporters not to vote by mail. Ballot/application ratio ~0.92. Small low-tail escape if only a partial mid-cycle figure is published by the 26 Nov cutoff. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmakers: none).

- Correos press room (checked 2026-11-16): 29N releases dated 6 Oct (applications open), 10 Nov (procedure; ballot papers mailed from 9 Nov), 16 Nov (applications deadline 19 Nov reminder). None contains any count of applications or ballots.
- labandera.es / herqles.com (2026-11-16): Interior has not published postal-vote application or ballot data; PP and Vox asked for daily Correos data to go to the Junta Electoral and candidacies, request unresolved.
- moncloa.com (2026-11-01): ~15,000 applications in the Comunitat Valenciana so far; bulk of applications typically arrive in the final two weeks before the deadline.
- Abascal (Vox), Oct 2026 (Infobae 2026-10-05): urges voters not to vote by post; Ayuso also cast doubt on it.
- Past general elections, Correos applications: Jun 2016 1,453,446; Apr 2019 1,346,995; Nov 2019 918,455 (infocostatropical); Jul 2023 2,622,808.
- Past general elections, ballots admitted: Apr 2019 1,241,716; Jun 2016 ~1.36M (search snippet; metric slightly unclear); Nov 2019 ~0.9M (900,188 'already sent' on deadline day 8 Nov 2019); Jul 2023 2,461,284 (night after deadline) then 2,471,935 (22 Jul, two days after the deadline).
- Ballots/applications ratio: 91-94% since 2008 (94.2% in 2023; Andalusia May 2026 91.58%).
- Recent regionals: Andalusia May 2026 178,540 applications (+1.1% vs 2022), 163,510 ballots; Extremadura Dec 2025 17,508 applications (-49% vs May 2023, which was combined with local elections), 16,193 ballots; Aragón Feb 2026 19,864 ballots; Castilla y León Mar 2026 54,316 applications.
- Publication timing pattern: Andalusia 2026 ballots release came the day after the deposit deadline (13 May -> 14 May); 2023 general the night after and two days after. Here deposit deadline is 25 Nov (Wed), cutoff is releases dated <=26 Nov. Nov 2019 precedent: a 'votes already sent' figure appeared on the deadline day itself, and a mid-cycle applications release quoted 322,140 votes admitted so far, i.e. partial figures do get published.
- Status quo: Correos publishes the applications total around 20-21 Nov, then the ballots-admitted total on 26 Nov.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off Correos' headline national cumulative ballots admitted/emitted/deposited/sent figure in the latest release dated <=26 Nov (Madrid time), not off application counts and not off a sum of regional/CERA breakdowns.
- Event window: Correos releases up to 26 Nov 2026 (deposit deadline 25 Nov); as of 2026-11-16 the ballot-deposit period (9-25 Nov) is ~45% elapsed and the publication window effectively closes 26 Nov.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
- Searched but not found: any national 29N application count to date; exact Dec 2015 postal figures; exact final Nov 2019 ballots-admitted total.
calls.reference_class: Postal ballots admitted by Correos in Spanish general elections held outside summer (2015-2019), with July 2023 as an upper regime marker

calls.reasoning: Non-summer general elections drew ~0.9-1.36M postal ballots; July 2023's 2.47M was a holiday outlier. The early Valencia pace (~15k applications by day 26, about 140k scaled nationally) is far below 2023's pace, and Andalusia's 2026 regional applications were flat. Vox's anti-postal messaging pushes down, while high salience and turnout push toward April 2019 levels. Correos usually releases the near-final count on the 25 Nov deadline or the day after, inside the cutoff. Small low-tail risk that only an interim figure is out by then. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the facts: no 29N counts published as of 16 Nov; Nov 2019 had ~918k applications and ~900k ballots; Apr 2019 had 1.24M; Jul 2023 had 2.47M (summer outlier); Valencia ~15k applications by 1 Nov; Andalusia 2026 flat; Correos usually publishes on or a day after the deadline. The disagreement is judgment about the level (medians 1.05M-1.32M) and how much weight the early Valencia pace deserves. That pace argues against Run 3's upper tail, but it is weak because applications are back-loaded. Salience and full turnout argue for a total above Nov 2019's ~0.9M, and the Vox boycott argues against. I kept the run-family reference class and took a ~1.1M median with a moderately wide spread. I retrieved nothing myself.

disagreements.verdict: Weak early-pace signal plus flat regional trend favors the lower-middle; took ~1.1M
